summary: Tested the new Outliers feature (Fanatics vs DK/FD/BetMGM/Hard Rock, NBA player-prop Overs) on the backend and frontend using live OddsBlaze data. I made no bets and no data changes. Backend: 7/7 pytest tests pass. The response shape is {rows, games, updated_at}. For every row (1176), pays_more matches decimal(price)/decimal(next_best)-1 within 1e-3 and is greater than 0. Rows are sorted by pays_more descending, books is between 1 and 4, next_book is one of the 4 books, and markets are within the 10 allowed. Every row's game is in the game strip, no row appears twice, and games are sorted by date. Frontend: the Outliers sidebar tab goes to /outliers, and the page renders 9 game cards and the table. A game card click filters the table (47 rows, all from that game) and syncs the game dropdown; a second click resets it to 541. The market filter works (rebounds 113, pts+reb+ast 73), and so does the books filter (1+ 1176, 2+ 541 by default, 3+ 292, All 4 143). The game dropdown filters, Refresh works, and the pays-more cell is green. The page threw no errors. Regression: /kalshi, /bets and /performance all load.

minor.issue: outliers._first_seen dict is never pruned (keyed by line+price), so it grows without limit in a long-running process. Prune keys that are no longer in the current scan.

If OddsBlaze returns non-200 (e.g. 429), an empty result is cached for the full 120s TTL, so that book silently drops out of the 'next best' comparison for 2 minutes. If this hits a non-Fanatics book, outliers can be overstated.

ui_bugs.issue: Math.round(pays_more*100) shows '0%' for edges under 0.5%. In the default 2+ view, 38 of 541 rows show 0%. Use one decimal place or a '<1%' label.

issues: Next best column shows only the price and book count. The name of the best book appears only in a title tooltip, so consider showing it inline.
The game strip has no visible scroll cue; the last card is cut off on the right at 1920px.

action_items: (Low) Show decimal or '<1%' for tiny pays_more
(Low) Don't cache failed (non-200) book fetches for the full TTL
critical_code_review_comments: outliers.py and Outliers.js are compact and correct. The key (away, home, norm_name, market, line) matches lines exactly across books.
Failed fetches are cached as empty for 120s
context_for_next_testing_agent: Outliers is a read-only page using live data. Run pytest normally, because pytest.ini adds xdist flags. Market filter testids replace non-word characters with '-' (e.g. outliers-market-filter-pts-reb-ast). Game filter testids look like outliers-game-filter-was-atl.
